Title: Risk prediction in IgA nephropathy: from conventional models to machine learning, deep learning, and precision nephrology
Summary: Reviews the evolution of risk-prediction modeling in IgA nephropathy, from conventional statistical models to machine learning and deep learning approaches. Discusses how these newer methods support a shift toward precision nephrology for individualized risk stratification.

Title: A machine learning-driven prognostic model based on peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets in osteosarcoma
Summary: Develops a prognostic model for osteosarcoma using peripheral blood lymphocyte subset data and a gradient boosting machine algorithm. The model achieved an AUC of 0.959 and effectively stratified patients into groups with significantly divergent survival outcomes.

Title: Machine learning-based prediction of 3-6-month post-stroke cognitive impairment using acute-phase clinical data: a two-center retrospective prognostic modeling study
Summary: A two-center retrospective study building machine learning models to predict cognitive impairment 3-6 months after stroke using clinical data collected in the acute phase. Aims to enable earlier identification of patients at risk of post-stroke cognitive decline.

Title: When to and when not to use machine learning in risk prediction models
Summary: A methodological commentary examining the circumstances under which machine learning offers genuine advantages over conventional statistical approaches for clinical risk prediction, and when it does not. Provides guidance for researchers deciding between modeling approaches.
Outcome: methodological guidance on risk prediction modeling

Title: Reliability and diagnostic performance of an automated MRI-based classifier compared with radiologists in Alzheimer's disease
Summary: Evaluates an automated MRI-based machine learning classifier for distinguishing cognitively normal individuals from Alzheimer's disease patients using standardized ADNI imaging data. Reports diagnostic performance comparable to expert radiologists.

Title: Automated Diagnosis of Breast Cancer Using Deep Learning Techniques Applied to Digital Mammography and Magnetic Resonance Images
Summary: Applies a hybrid of four pretrained CNN architectures (ResNet18, MobileNet, ShuffleNet, InceptionV3) via transfer learning to classify mammography and DCE-MRI images as normal, benign, or malignant. The ResNet-based model achieved the highest accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity among those tested.

Title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Diagnostic Radiology: A Paradigm Shift Toward Predictive Neuroimaging and Early Detection of Brain Disorders
Summary: Reviews how AI and machine learning are reshaping diagnostic radiology, particularly neuroimaging, moving practice from descriptive interpretation toward predictive, quantitative analysis. Focuses on applications for early detection of brain disorders.

Title: Explainable Transformer Models for Clinical Prediction Tasks on Structured Electronic Health Records
Summary: Presents BERT-LER, a BERT-style transformer model pretrained and fine-tuned on coded EHR timelines from a de-identified dataset of 75 million patients. Encodes lab results as discrete, percentile-binned tokens to preserve graded information while supporting explainable clinical prediction tasks.

Title: Explainable Machine Learning for Sepsis Outcome Prediction Using a Novel Romanian Electronic Health Record Dataset
Summary: Develops explainable machine learning models to predict sepsis outcomes using an EHR dataset of 12,286 hospitalizations from a large Romanian emergency hospital. The best-performing model for the deceased-versus-recovered outcome achieved an AUC of 0.983 and 93% accuracy.

Title: Building an interpretable machine learning prognosis prediction model based on baseline examinations of patients with esophageal cancer undergoing surgery
Summary: Builds an interpretable machine learning model using non-invasive baseline examination data to predict prognosis for esophageal cancer patients undergoing surgery. Aims to improve early prognostic assessment while keeping the model's predictions clinically interpretable.

Title: Development of a machine learning-based prognostic prediction model and a web-based tool for pediatric hepatoblastoma: a Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database study
Summary: Develops and compares several machine learning-based survival models for pediatric hepatoblastoma using the SEER database and creates an online prediction tool. Enables individualized survival probability estimation for children with this cancer.

Title: Machine learning-driven prognostic modeling in head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma: A retrospective cohort study
Summary: A retrospective cohort study building machine learning models to stratify risk and predict survival in patients with head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma. Compares model performance for individualized prognosis prediction.
Disease: head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma

Title: Machine learning-based prognostic model integrating preoperative HALP score and lactate dehydrogenase for predicting postoperative recurrence of prostate cancer
Summary: Develops a machine learning model integrating preoperative HALP score, lactate dehydrogenase, and clinicopathological features to predict postoperative recurrence of prostate cancer. Reports high accuracy for individualized recurrence risk prediction.

Title: Prognostic model for pancreatic cancer based on machine learning of routine slides and transcriptomic tumor analysis
Summary: Builds a prognostic model for pancreatic cancer that combines machine learning analysis of routine histopathology slides with transcriptomic tumor data. Aims to improve individualized prognosis prediction beyond conventional staging.

Title: Machine learning models based on XGBoost algorithm to predict prognosis of lung cancer brain metastases
Summary: Develops XGBoost-based machine learning models to predict prognosis for patients with lung cancer brain metastases, achieving AUC values of 0.805-0.822 in training and test sets. Demonstrates superior calibration and clinical net benefit compared to traditional prognostic algorithms.

Title: Era-specific prognostic factors and an interpretable machine-learning survival model for renal cell carcinoma brain metastases
Summary: Identifies era-specific prognostic factors and builds an interpretable machine learning survival model for patients with renal cell carcinoma brain metastases. Aims to provide clinically interpretable, up-to-date survival predictions.

Title: Development and evaluation of explainable machine learning models for predicting prognosis in patients with primary biliary cholangitis
Summary: Develops and validates explainable machine learning models using clinical and laboratory data to predict prognosis in patients with primary biliary cholangitis, comparing six different algorithms. Emphasizes model interpretability alongside predictive performance.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Diagnostic Model for Ocular Surface Neoplastic Diseases
Summary: Develops a deep learning model trained on 1,491 ocular surface images to diagnose seven ocular surface diseases including nevus, limbal dermoid, MALT lymphoma, ocular surface squamous neoplasia, melanoma, pinguecula, and pterygium. The model achieved a 96.0% positive predictive value, outperforming corneal specialists.

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning models for colorectal cancer detection in histopathological whole-slide images: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis
Summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of deep learning models for detecting colorectal cancer in histopathological whole-slide images. Finds high sensitivity and strong overall diagnostic discrimination across the pooled studies.

Title: Scalable Clinical Data Infrastructure and Comparative ML Evaluation for Hospitalisation Risk Prediction in Elderly Patients with Multiple Long-Term Conditions using CPRD
Summary: Builds a scalable clinical data infrastructure using the UK CPRD database and comparatively evaluates machine learning models, including deep learning patient-trajectory architectures, for predicting hospitalization risk in elderly patients with multiple long-term conditions. Finds that interpretable baseline models remain competitive with more complex black-box approaches.

Title: Retrieval-aligned Tabular Foundation Models Enable Robust Clinical Risk Prediction in Electronic Health Records Under Real-world Constraints
Summary: Presents AWARE, a task-aligned retrieval framework using supervised embedding learning and lightweight adapters to improve tabular in-context learning for clinical risk prediction across multi-cohort EHR and ICU datasets. AWARE improved AUPRC by roughly 0.3-4.0% as training size scales, up to 7.0% under high feature dimensionality, and up to 12.2% under extreme class imbalance versus classic retrieval methods.
Outcome: clinical risk prediction (AUPRC improvement under real-world constraints)

Title: Machine learning-based prediction of dataset-defined myocardial infarction risk: A retrospective computational study for precision cardiovascular risk assessment
Summary: Develops and compares machine learning and deep learning models (Random Forest, deep neural network, SVM) to predict myocardial infarction/heart disease risk from demographic, clinical, ECG, exercise-testing, and angiographic variables in 1,888 patient records. The Random Forest model performed best, achieving 97.0% accuracy and an ROC-AUC of 0.97.

Title: Development and Validation of a Novel Risk Prediction Model for Incident Diabetic Foot Complications: A Large, Longitudinal, Population-Based Machine Learning Study
Summary: Uses UK Biobank data on 502,175 participants (29,766 in the incident cohort with 1,252 diabetic foot complication events) to build the DFC-Clin machine learning model estimating diabetic foot complication risk across multiple time horizons. The model showed improved discrimination compared with existing approaches and was implemented as a web-based risk stratification tool.
Outcome: incident diabetic foot complication risk prediction

Title: Development of an Explainable Machine Learning Model to Predict Mortality Risk in Sepsis Patients: Insights From a Real-World Clinical Data
Summary: Develops an explainable, SHAP-interpretable machine learning model using real-world clinical data to predict mortality risk in sepsis patients. Aims to support individualized early risk stratification and clinical decision-making in the ICU.

Title: Development of a Machine Learning-Based Prognostic Model for Intermediate Trophoblastic Tumors: A Single-Center Study With Web-Based Tool Implementation
Summary: Analyzes a retrospective cohort of 236 patients with intermediate trophoblastic tumors, using Cox regression, LASSO, gradient boosting, and random survival forest (RSF) to identify predictors of progression-free survival. The final RSF model, based on FIGO stage, interval from antecedent pregnancy, Ki-67 index, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, was implemented as a web-based risk stratification tool.

Title: Multi-strategy feature selection and multi-model machine learning for prognostic prediction in primary gastric diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Summary: Analyzes 3,773 primary gastric diffuse large B-cell lymphoma patients from the SEER database, combining four feature-selection strategies (LASSO, Boruta, backward stepwise, best subset regression) with four ML algorithms. The XGBoost model built on best-subset-regression-selected predictors (age, stage, chemotherapy, marital status, income) achieved the best calibration and clinical net benefit, and was deployed as a web-based risk tool.

Title: A multidimensional risk prediction framework for malignant intestinal obstruction based on machine learning: computational model development and clinical validation
Summary: Develops a multimodal machine learning framework for malignant intestinal obstruction using Lasso-Boruta dual-modality feature screening and an XGBoost-Random Survival Forest cascade model incorporating a dynamic tumor enhancement ratio. The model achieved an AUC of 0.84 (± 0.03) and Brier score of 0.19 in internal validation, with robust performance on external validation.

Title: Development and internal-external validation of a machine learning-based risk prediction model for multidrug resistance in mechanically ventilated ICU patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Summary: Analyzes 477 mechanically ventilated ICU patients with COPD from the MIMIC-IV database, using Boruta and LASSO feature selection with seven machine learning algorithms to predict multidrug-resistant infection risk. The K-nearest neighbor model and an accompanying nomogram showed favorable predictive value and generalizability for early risk stratification.

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based model for predicting fall-related injury risk in hospitalized patients
Summary: Develops and compares four machine learning models (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, SVM) to predict which in-hospital falls will result in patient injury, supporting post-fall risk stratification. The Random Forest model performed best (AUC 0.814 training / 0.795 test), with SHAP analysis identifying low albumin and impaired transfer ability as major risk contributors.

Title: Multimodal deep learning model for prediction of prognosis in central nervous system inflammation
Summary: Develops a multimodal deep learning model integrating 3D brain MRI (segmented via FastSurfer and processed with a 3D CNN) with clinical features to predict prognosis in patients with CNS inflammation. The model outperformed unimodal approaches across aetiologies, achieving AUCs of 0.80 (autoimmune), 0.91 (bacterial), 1.00 (tuberculosis), and 0.92 (viral), and improved clinicians' prognostic accuracy when used as a decision aid.

Title: A machine learning-based risk prediction model for Hospitalized patients with deep vein thrombosis
Summary: Retrospectively analyzed 231 hospitalized patients (159 with DVT, 72 without) to develop and internally validate a machine learning risk-prediction model using LASSO-selected clinical/laboratory predictors and five algorithms (XGBoost, logistic regression, CatBoost, random forest, SVM). Model explainability techniques were used to identify the most influential predictors of DVT occurrence.
AI Technique: ML (XGBoost, CatBoost, Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression)

Title: A hybrid deep learning and large language model framework for MACE risk prediction and evidence-based clinical recommendations
Summary: Develops a two-part framework combining a 1D convolutional neural network that predicts individual risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) from structured EMR data, with a retrieval-augmented-generation LLM (Mistral) that translates the predicted risk into personalized, guideline-constrained lifestyle and preventive recommendations aligned with WHO/AHA standards. Delivered via a web interface combining accurate risk prediction with interpretable recommendations.
Outcome: MACE risk prediction plus personalized preventive recommendations

Title: Deep Learning-Based Risk Factor Analysis for Accurate Prediction of Lung Cancer in High-Risk Populations
Summary: Proposes a deep learning framework combining the LIDC-IDRI imaging dataset, a Whale Optimization/Adaptive Particle Swarm feature-selection algorithm, and CNN-based classifiers (including a kernel-based non-Gaussian CNN) for lung cancer risk stratification in high-risk populations. The optimized model achieved a prediction accuracy of 99.25%.
AI Technique: Deep learning (CNN / kernel-based non-Gaussian CNN with WOA-APSO feature optimization)

Title: Explainable deep-learning models to predict diaphragmatic dysfunction and cognitive stress in ICU patients under mechanical ventilation
Summary: A multicenter retrospective study of 25,751 mechanically ventilated ICU patients developed a multimodal, explainable deep-learning framework integrating diaphragm ultrasound with longitudinal bedside physiologic and treatment data to predict diaphragmatic dysfunction and high cognitive stress/delirium. Multimodal integration improved prediction over single-modality models, and post hoc explainability highlighted shared predictors suggestive of a lung-brain axis.
Outcome: prediction of diaphragmatic dysfunction and cognitive stress/delirium in ventilated ICU patients

Title: Deep transfer learning radiomics combined with explainable machine learning for predicting malignancy risk in parotid gland tumors based on ultrasound
Summary: Using ultrasound data from 1,191 patients across three centers, this study extracted radiomics and deep transfer learning features (ResNet50, Inception_V3, VGG19) and combined them with six explainable machine learning classifiers to predict preoperative malignancy risk in parotid gland tumors, using postoperative histopathology as the reference standard.
AI Technique: Deep learning (ResNet50, Inception_V3, VGG19 transfer learning) + ML (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, etc.)
Outcome: preoperative malignancy risk classification of parotid gland tumors

Title: A Deep Learning Model for Absolute Risk Prediction of Alcohol Use Disorder in Adolescents and Young Adults
Summary: Using data from the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health, this study developed the first deep learning model to provide personalized absolute risk estimates of developing alcohol use disorder among adolescents/young adults who use alcohol, with SHAP used to assess predictor importance (biological sex, delinquency, personality traits). The model achieved AUCs of 0.72 (cross-validation) and 0.85 (independent validation) for 6-year AUD risk.
Outcome: absolute risk prediction of alcohol use disorder (AUC 0.72-0.85)

Title: Research on a Deep Learning-Based Model for Predicting Malignancy Risk of Pan-Endocrine System across Thyroid and Breast Nodules
Summary: Built a Transformer-based multi-task deep learning model combining shared feature layers with organ-specific layers, trained on clinical data from patients with thyroid nodules (n=2,386) and breast nodules (n=2,753) across three hospitals, to jointly predict malignancy risk across both organs. The unified model achieved AUCs of 0.932 for thyroid nodules and 0.917 for breast nodules.
Outcome: malignancy risk classification for thyroid and breast nodules (AUC 0.932/0.917)

Title: Risk prediction of progression from normal cognitive function to Alzheimer's disease in elderly aged 65 and above based on deep learning methods
Summary: Compared DeepSurv, DeepHit, and Cox proportional hazards models to predict progression from normal cognitive function to Alzheimer's disease in elderly patients using easily obtainable early-stage predictors. The deep learning models showed better consistency than the Cox model (concordance indices of 0.82 and 0.83 vs. 0.81), supporting their use for early AD-risk screening pending clinical validation.

Title: Exploration of a Multimodal Machine Learning Model Integrating Ultrasound and Clinical Indicators for the Diagnosis of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
Summary: In 235 patients, this study combined ultrasound and clinical indicators to build and compare four machine learning models (logistic regression, XGBoost, random forest, SVM) for diagnosing diabetic peripheral neuropathy, using 10-fold cross-validation. The random forest model showed the best diagnostic performance and potential for clinical application in DPN risk assessment.
AI Technique: ML (Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, Logistic Regression)

Title: A Deep Learning-Based Multimodal Clinico-Histology-Genomic Prognostic Model in Prostate Cancer
Summary: Developed a deep learning framework that extracts histopathological features from H&E whole-slide images, predicts genomic and histopathological scores, and integrates these with clinical variables via Cox regression to generate a multimodal prognostic score for prostate cancer, trained on TCGA and externally validated on the PLCO trial. The multimodal score outperformed unimodal scores and NCCN risk stratification (C-index 0.774 vs. 0.706-0.746) and identified high-risk patients with markedly shorter progression-free intervals (HR 9.09) and worse cancer-specific mortality (HR 8.79).
AI Technique: Deep learning (multimodal: WSI + genomic + clinical, Cox regression)

Title: Development and external validation of an interpretable multimodal deep learning model for 5-year mortality in high-risk stage ii colorectal cancer
Summary: Developed and externally validated an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating clinical data, serum biomarkers, and venous-phase CT imaging to predict 5-year cancer-specific mortality in 778 high-risk stage II colorectal cancer patients across three centers (development n=720, external test n=58). The multimodal model improved 5-year mortality risk stratification over conventional approaches, supporting risk-adapted surveillance pending prospective validation.

Title: Multimodal deep learning for survival prediction and biomarker discovery in non-small cell lung cancer
Summary: Analyzed whole-slide imaging, next-generation sequencing, and clinical features from 2,366 NSCLC patients, developing a Sequential-Adapted Attention (SeAttn) model for histology plus deep learning models for genetic/clinical data, fused via a Cox-based multimodal approach. The SeAttn model achieved AUC 0.98 for histologic subtype prediction, and the combined multimodal model reached a C-index of 0.71 for 5-year prognosis, also identifying novel prognostic biomarkers.
AI Technique: Deep learning (multimodal: whole-slide imaging attention model + NGS + clinical, Cox-based fusion)

Title: Predicting Readmissions or Post-Discharge Mortality After Cardiac Surgery with Machine Learning Using an Australian Database
Summary: Developed machine learning models using the ANZSCTS Database (54 Australian hospitals, 2017-2021) to predict 30-day readmission or post-discharge mortality after CABG, valvular, or aortic surgery. Models showed only limited predictive ability (best AUROC 0.615 with a deep neural network), suggesting the registry needs additional variables, such as linked electronic medical record data, to build more accurate prediction models.
AI Technique: ML (deep neural network and other ML models, comparative)

Title: Predicting Intensive Care Readmission Among Hospitalized Children
Summary: Developed machine learning models using data from 35,601 pediatric patients across multiple sites to predict unplanned PICU readmission within 48 hours of transfer to the inpatient ward. Internal validation AUCs ranged 0.70-0.73 across four models, but performance dropped substantially on external validation (AUC 0.60-0.69), highlighting limited generalizability of locally derived pediatric readmission models.

Title: Machine Learning Prediction of Heart Failure Readmissions: Insights From a Multicenter Emergency Department Trial
Summary: In a sub-analysis of a cluster randomized clinical trial (n=14,131) across 12 South Australia emergency departments, an XGBoost model predicted 12-month heart failure readmission with AUC 0.861, outperforming logistic regression (0.846), random forest (0.845), LASSO (0.851), and neural networks (0.842). Findings support ML-based risk stratification for targeted preventive care after ED presentation.

Title: Prediction of Risk of Unplanned Readmission or Death in Elderly Heart Failure Patients During the Vulnerable Phase: Machine Learning With SHAP Interpretation
Summary: Built 18 predictive models using six ML algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, AdaBoost, GBDT, GNB, SVM) with three feature selection methods to predict readmission or death during the vulnerable phase in elderly heart failure patients, using SHAP for interpretation. The Boruta-XGBoost model performed best (AUC 0.873, sensitivity 0.839), with hemoglobin, free thyroxine, age, diabetes, and potassium as top predictors.
AI Technique: ML (XGBoost with Boruta feature selection; SHAP interpretation)
Outcome: unplanned readmission/death risk during vulnerable phase (AUC 0.873)

Title: Leveraging a machine learning model to predict hospital readmission risk: integrating clinical and social determinants of health data
Summary: Compared six ML algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, SVM) integrating clinical data with area-level social determinants of health to predict 30-day hospital readmission. XGBoost performed best (ROC-AUC 0.79), with neighborhood socioeconomic status and household composition emerging as important predictors alongside clinical variables.
AI Technique: ML (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression)

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning model and a web tool for predicting the risk of Crohn's disease diagnosis in Chinese patients
Summary: Using retrospective electronic medical record data from two Chinese tertiary hospitals (2020-2024), trained nine ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, gradient boosting machine, and neural network, to support preliminary diagnosis of Crohn's disease, then deployed the best-performing model as a public web-based tool.
AI Technique: ML (gradient boosting machine, among 9 algorithms compared)

Title: Machine learning in the diagnosis and prognosis of transient ischaemic attack: a systematic review
Summary: Systematic review of machine learning approaches for diagnosing and prognosticating transient ischemic attack, finding that models based on electronic health records or CT angiography radiomics achieved best-performing AUCs of 0.82-0.88.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Prognostic Models for Functional Outcomes in Spinal Cord Injury: Systematic Review
Summary: Systematic review of machine learning-based prognostic models predicting functional outcomes after spinal cord injury, finding that while ML is increasingly used for this purpose, existing evidence is limited by incomplete reporting, high risk of bias, and substantial heterogeneity across studies. Larger, methodologically robust studies with external validation are needed before clinical implementation.
Outcome: functional outcome prognosis after spinal cord injury

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for early risk prediction of acute myocardial infarction
Summary: Developed an interpretable ML model using multidimensional clinical data from 7,939 patients (Jan 2020-Jan 2024) for early risk prediction of acute myocardial infarction, using SHAP to select and interpret the top 10 predictive features.

Title: Machine learning risk prediction models for medication harm in hospitalised adult patients
Summary: Trained eight ML models on data from 279 hospitalized adult general medical/geriatric patients (40 of whom experienced 51 medication harm events) to predict medication harm risk. A random forest model performed best, achieving an AUC of 0.76, specificity of 0.90, and accuracy of 0.86.

Title: Predictive modeling for mortality risk in elderly patients with pulmonary embolism using machine learning algorithms
Summary: Developed and internally validated five ML models (decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, SVM, k-nearest neighbors) using data from 2013-2023 to predict in-hospital mortality in elderly patients with pulmonary embolism. ML-based models showed strong discriminative performance, supporting early identification of high-risk elderly PE patients for timely intervention.
AI Technique: ML (XGBoost, random forest, decision tree, SVM, k-NN)

Title: Machine Learning Models in the Prediction of Adverse Outcomes in Peripheral Arterial Disease: Meta-Analysis
Summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 studies comparing ML models to traditional regression for predicting adverse outcomes in peripheral arterial disease patients. Gradient boosted models showed the best performance (diagnostic odds ratio 36.6, sensitivity 0.853, specificity 0.863), consistently outperforming traditional regression, though only 23% of included studies performed external validation.
AI Technique: ML (gradient boosted models, among various algorithms)

Title: Creation and Verification of a Machine Learning-Based Model for Predicting Breast Cancer Risk in Patients with BI-RADS 4 Breast Lesions
Summary: Built and validated eight ML models using 216 BI-RADS 4 breast lesions (151 training/65 validation) to predict breast cancer risk, identifying six independent risk factors via LASSO/logistic regression and interpreting the optimal model with SHAP. A logistic regression model showed the most stable performance, while a random forest model showed signs of overfitting (AUC 1.00).
AI Technique: ML (logistic regression, random forest, among 8 algorithms)
Outcome: breast cancer risk prediction in BI-RADS 4 lesions

Title: Development and validation of an early risk prediction model based on inflammatory and metabolically derived markers for early diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease
Summary: Used inflammatory and metabolic markers from patients at two Chinese hospitals (209 training, 42 external validation) to build a machine learning-based early prediction model for diabetic kidney disease, applying feature selection and multi-model comparison to achieve high diagnostic precision.

Title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models to Optimize Imaging and Referrals for Dizziness in the Emergency Department
Summary: Trained four ML models (decision tree, LASSO logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost) on 6,637 ED patients with dizziness/vertigo/imbalance (2014-2022) to predict serious 30-day diagnoses (stroke, TIA, dissection, brain tumor). LASSO logistic regression showed the best balance of discrimination (AUC 0.97, sensitivity 97%, specificity 91%), with projected reductions in CT utilization of 53-85% versus current practice.
Disease: stroke, transient ischemic attack, vertebral artery dissection, brain tumor
AI Technique: ML (LASSO logistic regression, XGBoost, random forest, decision tree)

Title: Machine Learning Approaches for Mortality Prediction in ARDS
Summary: Compared multiple ML models to predict 90-day all-cause mortality and 28-day hospital mortality in ARDS patients, with models achieving AUCs of 0.715-0.753 and 0.693-0.721 respectively. XGBoost achieved the most consistent balance of AUC, recall, and F1 score across both outcomes.

Title: Machine Learning Prediction of Early In-Hospital Mortality in Lung Cancer Patients Using Administrative Data
Summary: Used administrative data to build ML models predicting early in-hospital mortality in lung cancer patients. XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.787 at baseline, improving to 0.791 with engineered features, outperforming logistic regression (0.783) and random forest (0.769).

Title: Development and validation of machine learning-based in-hospital mortality predictive models for acute aortic syndrome in emergency departments
Summary: Developed and externally validated ML models using 34 clinical variables from 929 patients (with 210 in an external test set) across three Chinese hospitals to predict in-hospital mortality in acute aortic syndrome, achieving internal/external AUCs of 0.85-0.90/0.73-0.85. A simplified five-variable model retained reasonable performance (AUC 0.71-0.86 internal, 0.75-0.78 external) for rapid clinical use.

Title: Deep learning-based in-hospital mortality prediction using long-term sequential data in ICU patients: a multi-center validation study
Summary: Multi-center validation study developing a deep learning model that integrates long-term historical ICU temporal clinical sequences and ICD diagnostic codes with current-admission data to predict in-hospital all-cause mortality, applicable to both single- and multiple-admission ICU patients. The approach improved on prior models that relied only on short-term single-hospitalization physiological data and lacked external validation.
Outcome: in-hospital mortality prediction in ICU patients

Title: Deep Learning for Ultrasound-Based Auxiliary Diagnosis of Emergency Ascites
Summary: Developed a Transformer-based deep learning model for automated detection of free intraperitoneal fluid in FAST ultrasound examinations for emergency ascites. The model achieved diagnostic performance comparable to a junior sonographer and significantly improved detection accuracy among non-specialist operators.
Outcome: automated free fluid/ascites detection on ultrasound

Title: A deep learning algorithm for coronary heart disease prediction based on retinal fundus photographs and optical coherence tomography
Summary: Developed and validated a multimodal deep learning algorithm integrating retinal fundus photographs and OCT images with clinical risk factors (via a nomogram) to assess coronary heart disease risk, using data from 505 patients (282 with CHD). The model achieved AUCs of 0.9954 (training), 0.9834 (validation), and 0.9138 (test cohort).

Title: Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Detection and Diagnosis System for Malignant Biliary Stricture (With Video)
Summary: Retrospective multicenter study (149 patients for development/internal validation, 25 for external validation) building a two-part deep learning system for digital cholangioscopy: a YOLOv11-based CADe model to localize suspicious mucosal/vascular features and a ResNet-18 CADx classifier (with Grad-CAM interpretability) to diagnose malignant biliary stricture. The CADe system achieved 91.2% mean average precision, 92.0% precision, and 87.0% recall.
Outcome: malignant biliary stricture detection/diagnosis on cholangioscopy

Title: Integrated imaging-informed and machine learning-based prognostic models for risk stratification in connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease: a multicenter study
Summary: Multicenter study comparing traditional ILD-GAP scoring, a composite GAP-plus-fibrosis-score model, and a machine learning model using clinical and imaging variables to risk-stratify patients with connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease. The integrated imaging-informed and machine learning approaches improved prognostic discrimination over physiology-based ILD-GAP scoring alone.
Disease: connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease

Title: Interpretable machine learning prognostication of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors across Chinese and United States cohorts
Summary: Compared six survival models (Cox regression, LASSO Cox, random survival forest, gradient-boosted survival analysis, Extra Trees, DeepSurv) in 337 patients with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (236 training, 101 test), with external validation on a SEER cohort. Extra Trees showed the best internal discrimination/calibration while DeepSurv had the highest external C-index; SHAP analysis identified core prognostic variables for a clinical nomogram.
AI Technique: ML (Extra Trees, DeepSurv, random survival forest, LASSO Cox, gradient-boosted survival analysis)

Title: Construction and validation of a prognostic model for clinical outcomes in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness based on multidimensional indicators: a prospective cohort study
Summary: Prospective cohort study of 304 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness using demographics, etiology, GCS/FOUR/CRS-R behavioral scores, and lab indicators to predict long-term functional outcome (GOS-E). A gradient boosting machine model was selected as the optimal predictor, providing decision support for clinicians.

Title: Gene expression-based machine learning model for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response prediction in hepatocellular carcinoma: a retrospective study
Summary: Retrospective study establishing a 10-gene expression signature (TOP2A, CDK1, CYP3A4, MASP2, EPHX2, HAO1, RACGAP1, GLYAT, ADH1B, CYP4A11) via machine learning to diagnose early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma and predict prognosis and treatment response. The model achieved AUC >0.9 for diagnosis, with high-risk scores associated with poor survival and differential response to sorafenib (AUC 0.791) versus TACE (AUC 0.768).

Title: Development and evaluation of a machine learning-based risk prediction model for enteral feeding intolerance in sepsis patients
Summary: Developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict enteral feeding intolerance (EFI) in septic patients, identifying APACHE II score, intra-abdominal pressure, and age as the primary predictive factors, followed by albumin levels, CRRT treatment, and enteral nutrition initiation timing. The model can help clinicians identify high-risk patients for individualized nutrition therapy.

Title: Deep learning for prognostic stratification and biomarker exploration in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
Summary: Multicenter retrospective study of 805 patients using a prior knowledge-guided deep learning system (MacroContextNet and PGCA-Net) on whole-slide histopathology images, segmenting eight tissue types to derive AI biomarkers and predict overall survival in upper tract urothelial carcinoma. PGCA-Net achieved C-index values of 0.672-0.795, with tumor-muscle and tumor-renal parenchyma co-localization scores associated with higher mortality risk.
AI Technique: Deep learning (whole-slide image models: MacroContextNet, PGCA-Net)

Title: Machine learning-based prognostic model and single-cell transcriptomic integration for identifying brain metastasis-associated malignant subpopulations and potential therapeutic targets in lung adenocarcinoma
Summary: Integrated single-cell RNA-seq data from lung adenocarcinoma brain metastasis samples with inferCNV/hdWGCNA analysis to identify brain-metastasis-associated core genes, then built a prognostic model using 101 combinations of 10 machine learning algorithms validated across LUAD cohorts. The model identified SEC61G and CFL1 as candidate biomarkers with experimental validation supporting their therapeutic relevance.
Outcome: prognosis/survival prediction and brain metastasis biomarker identification

Title: Multimodal data driven machine learning approach for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in pulmonary disease management within primary healthcare settings
Summary: Proposed the Probabilistic Agent Driven Diagnostic Model (PADDM), integrating a Manifold Constrained Feature Encoder, an Agent Based Decision Planner, and an Uncertainty Propagation Regularizer to support multimodal diagnostic decision-making for pulmonary disease in primary care. Evaluated across respiratory physiological signals, symptom records, and diagnostic evidence, PADDM improved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score over baseline methods.

Title: Study of a Kawasaki disease diagnostic prediction model based on the LightGBM machine learning algorithm
Summary: Retrospectively analyzed pre-treatment clinical data from 4,469 pediatric patients (2,345 with Kawasaki disease, 2,124 febrile non-KD controls) to build a LightGBM diagnostic model with SHAP-based interpretation. The simplified LightGBM model achieved an AUC of 0.9792, with 93.4% accuracy, 92.77% sensitivity, and 94.10% specificity at the standard threshold.

Title: Explainable machine-learning model for coronary artery disease diagnosis in non-AMI patients: integrating inflammatory and traditional risk factors
Summary: Retrospectively analyzed 4,656 patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD, using LASSO regression to select 21 candidate features (demographic, clinical, biochemical, and inflammatory cytokines) and training 10 ML algorithms. The generalized linear model was selected as final (AUC=0.815), with SHAP analysis identifying hypertension, hyperlipidemia, sex, triglycerides, and interleukin-6 as top predictors.
AI Technique: ML (generalized linear model, SHAP-interpreted; compared across 10 algorithms)

Title: Development and validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting acute kidney injury in critically ill patients with primary peritonitis: a multicenter cohort study
Summary: Used a derivation cohort (n=329) and an external validation cohort (n=367, MIMIC-IV) to select 15 features via the Boruta algorithm and train 12 machine learning approaches for predicting primary peritonitis-associated acute kidney injury (PPA-AKI). A Stepglm[both] + gradient boosting machine combination was identified as the superior algorithm for predicting PPA-AKI risk.
AI Technique: ML (Stepglm + gradient boosting machine, ensemble of 12 algorithms)

Title: Diagnostic Performance of Machine Learning for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Jan 2014-Apr 2026) of machine learning and deep learning models across three SLE-related tasks: SLE classification/diagnosis, lupus nephritis diagnosis, and neuropsychiatric SLE discrimination. ML models showed promising diagnostic accuracy, but wide prediction intervals, limited external validation, and high risk of bias in 22 of 29 (75.9%) studies restrict conclusions about real-world generalizability.
Disease: systemic lupus erythematosus, lupus nephritis, neuropsychiatric SLE

Title: A Deep Learning Breast Cancer Risk Model for Precise Supplemental Screening
Summary: Multisite cohort study of 123,091 screening mammograms in 67,019 women 30 years or older comparing a deep learning breast cancer risk model against breast-density-based criteria. The DL model showed greater accuracy than breast density in estimating future breast cancer risk and better stratified false-negative screening results, supporting its use as a more precise trigger for supplemental imaging access.
Outcome: future breast cancer risk stratification/false-negative screening rate

Title: Deep learning-driven MRI radiomics reveals biological subtypes and predicts recurrence risk in rectal cancer
Summary: Multicenter study of 2,060 rectal cancer patients without neoadjuvant therapy across four cohorts, using unsupervised clustering of deep-learning-extracted MRI radiomic features to identify three biologically distinct subtypes with differing immune phenotypes and prognosis. A recurrence risk scoring system combined with clinical variables improved 5-year recurrence-free survival prediction, raising AUC from 0.799 to 0.834 (training) and 0.780 to 0.825 (external validation).

Title: Multimodal Deep Learning with Routine Clinical Data for Recurrence Risk Stratification in HR+/HER2- Early Breast Cancer
Summary: Developed the MRRP model, a hierarchical transformer-based fusion framework integrating whole-slide pathology images, ultrasound imaging and reports, and structured clinical parameters, to stratify recurrence risk in 768 HR+/HER2- early breast cancer patients. MRRP achieved superior prognostic performance (C-index=0.840) versus single-modality models, with time-dependent AUCs exceeding 0.85 at 3 and 5 years.

Title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Machine Learning Models in Predicting Functional Outcome of Thrombectomy for Acute Posterior Circulation Artery Occlusion: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of five studies (1,739 patients) evaluating machine learning models predicting favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation artery occlusion. The best-performing models, including random forest, achieved good discrimination (AUC up to 0.93, accuracy up to 0.8), supporting ML's potential for personalized post-thrombectomy risk stratification.
AI Technique: ML (random forest and other classifiers, meta-analysis)

Title: Evaluation of coronary heart disease risk prediction based on simple physical examination parameters by machine learning model: a retrospective cohort model development and validation study
Summary: Retrospective cohort study using Framingham Heart Study data (internal) and an external hospital cohort to develop a stacked ensemble ML model (gradient boosting, random forest, XGBoost with logistic-regression meta-learner) predicting coronary heart disease risk from 10 simple physical-exam parameters. The model achieved AUC 0.977 internally and AUC 0.929 on external validation, supporting low-cost CHD screening.
AI Technique: ML (stacked ensemble: gradient boosting, random forest, XGBoost)

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for predicting postherpetic neuralgia risk
Summary: Developed and externally validated ML models predicting postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) after herpes zoster using a training cohort of 627 patients and an external validation cohort of 219 patients. XGBoost performed best, achieving AUC 0.826 in training and 0.840 in external validation, with age, antiviral therapy timing, and acute pain severity as top predictors via SHAP analysis.

Title: Development and validation of a parsimonious and noninvasive clinical decision machine learning model for predicting the risk of long-term mild cognitive impairment in older adults: A multinational cohort study
Summary: Multinational cohort study developing a parsimonious ML model using five noninvasive baseline predictors (age, sex, education, instrumental activities of daily living, and others) to predict long-term risk of mild cognitive impairment in older adults. The model generalized well on external validation, achieving AUC 0.786 in the ELSA cohort and AUC 0.745 in the HRS cohort, with an interactive SHAP-based web tool for primary-care screening.

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for early risk prediction of acute myocardial infarction
Summary: Study of 7,939 patients from a Chinese hospital (2020-2024) using 108-dimensional clinical and biochemical features to build an interpretable ML model for early acute myocardial infarction risk prediction, with SHAP analysis narrowing to the top 10 features for a simplified, clinically usable model.

Title: Machine learning-based prediction of early invasive mechanical ventilation in ICU patients with pneumonia: Development and external validation
Summary: Developed and externally validated an ML model and online calculator predicting early invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) need in ICU pneumonia patients. LightGBM was the best-performing model, achieving AUC 0.799 in internal testing and AUC 0.702 in external validation (n=155), offering an interpretable tool for early risk stratification.
Outcome: need for early invasive mechanical ventilation

Title: AI-Enabled Modeling for Alzheimer's Disease Risk Prediction and Validation
Summary: Developed and validated multiple AI models (random forest, XGBoost, deep learning) integrating multimodal clinical, CSF biomarker, and cognitive-assessment data for Alzheimer's disease risk stratification. The random forest model performed best, achieving AUC 0.899 in training and 0.879 in validation, with CSF p-tau181/Abeta42 ratio and APOE epsilon4 genotype as key risk features.
AI Technique: ML (random forest, XGBoost, deep learning comparison)

Title: Development and Validation of a Novel Risk Prediction Model for Incident Diabetic Foot Complications: A Large, Longitudinal, Population-Based Machine Learning Study
Summary: Used UK Biobank data on 502,175 participants (29,766 forming an incident cohort with 1,252 diabetic foot complication events) to build the DFC-Clin machine learning model via fivefold cross-validation and leave-one-center-out validation. The model showed improved discrimination over existing approaches and provides multi-time-horizon risk estimates for incident diabetic foot complications.
Outcome: incident diabetic foot complication risk prediction

Title: A next-generation prediction risk model for acute myocardial infarction: Derivation and validation in a multi-centre cohort
Summary: Analyzed 382,589 patients and 3.9 million EHR encounters from an integrated Colombian cardiovascular cohort, following TRIPOD+AI guidance, to build a model combining a calibrated gradient-boosting classifier with an interpretable survival ensemble (Cox regression, random survival forests, discrete-time hazards) predicting 6- and 12-month acute myocardial infarction risk. The classifier achieved AUC 0.869, with survival models reaching C-indices of 0.83.
AI Technique: ML (gradient boosting + survival ensemble: Cox regression, random survival forests)

Title: Development of a machine learning-based prognostic prediction model and a web-based tool for pediatric hepatoblastoma: a Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database study
Summary: SEER-based study of 614 pediatric hepatoblastoma patients (2000-2021) comparing machine learning survival models, with Random Survival Forest performing best (AUC 0.822/0.810/0.809 for 1-/3-/5-year survival in training; 0.740/0.765/0.765 in validation). Identified age, tumor size, lymph-node invasion, metastatic status, surgery, and chemotherapy as key prognostic factors, and deployed a web-based prediction tool.

Title: Prognostic model for pancreatic cancer based on machine learning of routine slides and transcriptomic tumor analysis
Summary: Trained a deep-learning model on archival histologic whole-slide images from 591 resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients, with external validation on 302 patients across multiple cohorts, to predict postoperative recurrence directly from routine slides. The model accurately predicted recurrence and revealed histologic image features correlated with gene-expression-based tumor biology.

Title: Development and external validation of machine-learning models for diagnosing malignant pleural effusion
Summary: Developed and externally validated ML models using routine pleural fluid and serum tumor markers to distinguish malignant from benign pleural effusion. The XGBoost model performed best, achieving AUC 0.988 (95% CI 0.982-0.993), accuracy 0.951, sensitivity 0.891, and specificity 0.984 in the training set.
Outcome: diagnosis of malignant vs benign pleural effusion

Title: Machine Learning-Based Prognostic Scoring for Spinal Metastases: A JASA Multicenter Prospective Study Integrating Modern Oncologic Advances
Summary: Multicenter prospective study by the Japan Association of Spine Surgeons with Ambition of 401 patients who underwent surgery for spinal metastases at 35 centers (2018-2021). Using LASSO logistic regression, identified five predictors of 1-year survival (age >=75, poor performance status, other bone metastases, preoperative opioid use, low Vitality Index); observed 1-year survival was 67.1%, aiming to better reflect modern oncologic therapies than older scoring systems.

Title: A machine learning-based online prediction model for recurrence risk in patients with Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess: a multicenter retrospective study
Journal/Source: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
Summary: Multicenter retrospective study built a hyperparameter-optimized XGBoost model integrating 9 clinical/laboratory predictors (including diabetes, malignancy, biliary disease, fibrinogen, procalcitonin, SOFA-2 score) to predict recurrence of Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess. The model achieved AUC 0.936 (training), 0.868 (internal test), and 0.904 (external validation), and was deployed as a public web-based prediction tool.

Title: XGBoost-based model for predicting five-year survival in gastric cancer using clinical indicators
Summary: Analyzed 2,270 gastric cancer patients using 20 clinical features to build an XGBoost model predicting five-year survival. The model achieved AUC 0.855 in the test cohort and effectively separated high- and low-risk patients, with pTNM stage and CA125 level as the most influential predictors.

Title: Development and internal validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting textbook outcome after free flap reconstruction in oral cancer
Summary: Single-center retrospective study of 752 oral cancer patients undergoing radical resection with immediate free flap reconstruction (2017-2025) built an explainable XGBoost model predicting "textbook outcome" (a composite of no 31-day mortality/readmission, length of stay <=21 days, no major complications, negative margins, adequate neck dissection). The model achieved AUC 0.843 and may support perioperative risk stratification.

Title: Explainable XGBoost model and nomogram for risk factor identification and risk prediction in cerebral small vessel disease: a machine learning-based retrospective cohort study
Summary: Retrospective cohort of 1,640 adults used LASSO regression and stepwise elimination to select 10 predictors (including blood glucose, hypertension history, systolic blood pressure, age, triglycerides, stroke history) for an explainable XGBoost model with an accompanying nomogram. The model achieved 88.0% accuracy, 80.9% sensitivity, and 93.8% specificity (F1 0.86) for identifying cerebral small vessel disease risk.

Title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study
Summary: Retrospective study of 1,026 hypertensive patients (718 development, 308 internal validation) built a deep neural network using time-in-target-range metrics derived from 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to identify patients at high risk for coronary heart disease. The model achieved AUC 0.822 in training and 0.796 in internal validation, outperforming conventional statistical approaches at modeling nonlinear relationships.
Outcome: coronary heart disease risk in hypertensive patients

Title: An interpretable machine learning framework with clinical nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute ischemic stroke using high-granularity bedside data
Summary: Built an ensemble gradient-boosting (CatBoost) model integrating bedside nursing assessments with emergency and laboratory data to predict early in-hospital mortality in acute ischemic stroke, outperforming established ICU scores. A simplified 10-feature nomogram achieved external AUC 0.871 with excellent calibration (Brier 0.098-0.114), and predictive validity held even using only the first 0-12 hours of data (external AUC 0.873).

Title: Interpretable gradient boosting machine model for predicting in-hospital mortality in sepsis-induced myocardial injury: a multicenter development, validation, and web-based clinical implementation
Summary: Multicenter study evaluated eight ML algorithms to predict in-hospital mortality in sepsis-induced myocardial injury, with a Gradient Boosting Machine model performing best (internal validation AUC 0.751, 95% CI 0.614-0.867), outperforming SVM (0.733) and logistic regression (0.730); the model was deployed on a web-based clinical platform for early risk assessment.

Title: Beyond Binary Cutoffs: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Individualized Diagnostic Reasoning in Suspected Urolithiasis
Summary: Trained a gradient boosting classifier on 17 continuous clinical and laboratory features to support individualized diagnostic reasoning for suspected urolithiasis in the emergency department, using Shapley-based explanations. The model achieved AUC 0.771 (95% CI 0.726-0.813) versus AUC 0.723 for an established reference scoring system, functioning as an interpretive adjunct rather than a replacement for CT imaging.

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for early risk prediction of acute myocardial infarction
Summary: Retrospective cohort of 7,939 patients from the Second Hospital of Shandong University (2020-2024) used 108 clinical and biochemical features to build an interpretable ML model for early acute myocardial infarction (AMI) risk prediction, with SHAP analysis identifying Hs-cTnI, NT-proBNP, and LDL-C as top predictors. The model achieved 93.2% accuracy on an independent validation set and was deployed via an interactive webserver.

Title: Exploration of a Multimodal Machine Learning Model Integrating Ultrasound and Clinical Indicators for the Diagnosis of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
Summary: Study of 235 patients built four ML models (logistic regression, XGBoost, random forest, and SVM) combining ultrasound and clinical indicators to diagnose diabetic peripheral neuropathy, using 10-fold cross-validation on a 7:3 train/test split. The random forest model showed the best diagnostic performance (AUC 0.852), supporting its potential for clinical DPN risk assessment.
AI Technique: ML (Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, logistic regression)

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning model and a web tool for predicting the risk of Crohn's disease diagnosis in Chinese patients
Summary: Dual-center retrospective study using electronic medical records from two Chinese tertiary hospitals developed a gradient boosting machine model from 10 predictive features to support early Crohn's disease diagnosis and referral. The model achieved AUROC 0.954 in the internal test cohort and 0.944 on external validation (196 patients), with a well-calibrated Brier score of 0.094, and was deployed as a web-based risk calculator.

Title: Creation and Verification of a Machine Learning-Based Model for Predicting Breast Cancer Risk in Patients with BI-RADS 4 Breast Lesions
Summary: Single-center study at Affiliated Hospital 2 of Nantong University tested eight ML algorithms to predict breast cancer risk in BI-RADS 4 lesions. Random forest showed signs of overfitting (AUC 1.00), while logistic regression proved more stable and was selected as the final model, with an accompanying nomogram built to support earlier breast cancer identification.
Outcome: breast cancer risk in BI-RADS 4 lesions

Title: Interpretable Machine Learning Models for Early Detection of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Using Non-Invasive Routine Clinical and Laboratory Data
Summary: Study of 152 patients at Fu Jen Catholic University Hospital in Taiwan compared ten interpretable ML models using 17 routine non-invasive clinical and anthropometric variables, calibrated against quantitative MRI-PDFF, to detect metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The best model, integrating the Fatty Liver Index and Hepatic Steatosis Index, achieved AUC 0.873, with SHAP identifying HSI, body fat composition, age, and triglycerides as top predictors.

Title: Development and validation of an early risk prediction model based on inflammatory and metabolically derived markers for early diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease
Summary: Study using 209 training and 42 external validation cases built an XGBoost-based model integrating inflammatory and metabolic markers (e.g., triglyceride-glucose index, systemic immune-inflammation index, neutrophil-to-albumin ratio) for early diabetic kidney disease diagnosis. The model demonstrated high-precision early detection compared with traditional clinical methods.

Title: Interpretable machine learning prediction models for 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation and acute kidney injury
Summary: Retrospective study using MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD databases compared nine ML algorithms to predict 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with coexisting atrial fibrillation and acute kidney injury, selecting the best model by AUC and validating it externally. SHAP-based interpretability and an online risk calculator were developed to support clinical use in this high-risk ICU population.

Title: Predicting short-term mortality in severe cirrhosis: An interpretable machine learning model integrating routine clinical indicators
Summary: Retrospective cohort of 1,044 MIMIC-IV patients (740 training, 304 validation) used multivariable logistic regression to identify eight independent predictors of 30-day mortality in severe cirrhosis, including age, INR, creatinine, platelets, WBC, bilirubin, and AST/ALT ratio. The resulting interpretable model outperformed traditional prognostic scores, with each unit rise in INR associated with a 42.3% increase in mortality risk.

Title: Explainable machine learning-based mortality prediction in critically ill patients with rheumatoid arthritis-associated lung disease: a radiomics and clinical data integration study
Summary: Retrospective study using MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR data (1,951 chest X-rays from 984 rheumatoid arthritis patients) built clinical-only, radiomics-only, and combined ML models with Boruta feature selection to predict ICU mortality risk in rheumatoid arthritis-associated lung disease. The integrated clinical-plus-radiomics model showed the best generalizability and interpretability for mortality prediction in this high-risk population.
AI Technique: ML (radiomics + clinical feature integration, Boruta selection)

Title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Mortality Risk and Survival Time in Lung Cancer Patients Treated with EGFR-TKIs
Summary: Using EHR data from three Taipei Medical University-affiliated hospitals, researchers built both a binary mortality classification model and a time-to-event survival model for lung cancer patients treated with EGFR-TKIs. The best classification model achieved AUC approximately 0.82 and the survival model a concordance index of approximately 0.66, supporting the use of multi-institution EHR data for prognostic modeling.
Outcome: mortality risk and survival time prediction

Title: Machine-Learning Based Prognostic Model for Predicting Early Recurrence in HCC Patients After Hepatectomies: An Explainable AI Approach
Summary: Developed an XGBoost-based explainable machine learning model to predict early recurrence after hepatectomy in hepatocellular carcinoma patients. The model showed robust discriminative generalizability for categorical risk stratification across multiple centers, despite expected calibration shifts between cohorts.

Title: Exploring prognostic factors in breast cancer: development and selection of optimal machine learning models
Summary: Compared multiple machine learning models, including Random Forest, to identify and select the optimal approach for uncovering prognostic factors in breast cancer. Ensemble methods, particularly Random Forest, showed superior predictive power for identifying key prognostic factors compared to the other models tested.
Outcome: identification of prognostic factors / survival prediction

Title: A Machine Learning-based Prognostic Stratification Model for Liver Cancer: Results from Survival Studies Using SEER Database
Summary: Used the SEER database to develop a machine learning-based prognostic stratification model for liver cancer survival. The model supports risk-based stratification of patients using population-level cancer registry data.

Title: An Online Machine Learning Algorithm-Based Prognostic Predictive Model for Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients
Summary: Enrolled 601 maintenance hemodialysis patients from Shantou Central Hospital to build a precise, user-friendly online machine learning-based mortality risk prediction model, later integrated into a web application. The tool is intended to support individualized prognostic risk assessment for maintenance hemodialysis patients.

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model using routine laboratory biomarkers to stratify severe pneumonia risk in young children
Summary: Retrospective cohort of 85,886 children with pneumonia (2013-2023) at a Chinese tertiary hospital used an interpretable CatBoost model on 57 admission laboratory biomarkers to simultaneously diagnose severe pneumonia and predict progression risk during hospitalization. Chloride and glucose emerged as novel high-risk biomarkers, with the model deployed as a web tool though it still needs external validation.
Outcome: severe pneumonia diagnosis and progression risk prediction

Title: AI-driven diagnosis of mpox using deep learning models
Summary: Built a leakage-aware benchmark for binary mpox classification from skin lesion images, combining the MSLD v1.0 and v2.0 datasets. Compared seven pretrained deep learning backbones and a weighted ensemble, with the ensemble achieving the best performance (accuracy 87.29%, F1-score 0.8334, AUC 0.9388).
AI Technique: Deep learning (ensemble of pretrained CNN backbones)

Title: Comparative evaluation of deep learning models for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and classification
Summary: Systematically compared low-complexity deep learning architectures (CNN, LSTM, MLP, CNN-MLP, ConvLSTM) for multi-class ECG-based cardiovascular disease diagnosis using the PTB Diagnostic ECG dataset, incorporating discrete wavelet transform feature extraction. The models balanced diagnostic accuracy with computational efficiency for noninvasive CVD classification from ECG signals.
AI Technique: Deep learning (CNN, LSTM, MLP, CNN-MLP, ConvLSTM)

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for the early diagnosis of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome: a retrospective cohort study
Summary: Retrospective cohort study compared seven machine learning algorithms to diagnose invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). The Random Forest model performed best, using five features (sex, serum potassium, INR, galactomannan positivity, SFTSV RNA load) to achieve an AUC of 0.871.
Disease: invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome
Outcome: early diagnosis of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis

Title: Development and verification of a comprehensive diagnostic model for osteosarcoma using random forest and artificial neural network
Summary: Study built diagnostic models for osteosarcoma using random forest and artificial neural network algorithms on clinical/laboratory data, with performance assessed in training and validation cohorts. The diagnostic model achieved AUCs of 0.826 and 0.766 in the training and validation groups respectively.

Title: Machine learning-driven dynamic prognosis for primary colorectal lymphoma
Summary: Using 2,743 patients with primary colorectal lymphoma from the SEER database (2004-2021), researchers identified seven prognostic variables and built a dynamic conditional-survival nomogram for individualized prognosis. The nomogram showed strong calibration with AUCs of 0.780, 0.789, and 0.812 for 3-, 5-, and 10-year survival prediction in the training cohort.

Title: Development and validation of a Random Forest prediction model integrating clinical and ultrasound radiomics features for microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma patients: a retrospective study
Summary: Retrospective study combined clinical characteristics with ultrasound radiomics features in a Random Forest model to preoperatively predict microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma patients. The model showed favorable predictive performance using a cost-effective, radiation-free ultrasound-based approach, offering an alternative to CT/MRI radiomics for surgical planning.

Title: A radiology-based differential diagnostic model for pelvic chondrosarcoma using random forest algorithms
Summary: In 238 patients (39.5% with pelvic chondrosarcoma), seven clinical and radiological features were used to build a random forest differential diagnostic model, validated in a held-out test cohort of 71 patients. The model achieved 96.6% sensitivity, 90.5% specificity, and 93.0% accuracy, offering a noninvasive alternative to biopsy.

Title: Development and validation of a diagnostic model for malignant pleural effusion based on random forest
Summary: Retrospective study of 1,239 adults undergoing diagnostic thoracentesis developed an eight-feature random forest model (including pleural fluid adenosine deaminase, CEA, cell count, and LDH) to identify malignant pleural effusion. The model achieved an AUC of 0.940 in the test set, outperforming single-marker approaches.

Title: Accurate Lung Cancer Prediction From CT Scans Using Advanced Deep Learning Methods
Summary: Proposed a multistage deep learning framework for lung cancer prediction from CT scans, combining hybrid graph convolutional network/conditional random field segmentation with capsule networks, Siamese networks, and a hybrid CNN-Transformer-GNN classifier. The approach achieved 91% accuracy, outperforming LSTM (80%), FNN (70%), and RNN (70%) baselines while reducing false positives.
Outcome: lung cancer classification from CT imaging

Title: A Machine Learning-Based Nomogram for Predicting Overall Survival in BCLC Stage 0-B Hepatocellular Carcinoma Patients with Low HALP Score
Summary: Analysis of 1,281 BCLC stage 0-B hepatocellular carcinoma patients found that a low HALP (hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet) score identified a subgroup with significantly higher 5-year mortality (59.7% vs 45.0%). A machine learning-based nomogram developed specifically for this low-HALP subgroup achieved AUCs of 0.73-0.83 across derivation and validation cohorts for 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival.

Title: A Clinical and Biomarker-Based Model for Predicting in-Hospital Mortality in Patients Undergoing Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Machine Learning-Based Nomogram Study
Summary: A retrospective cohort of 122 ECMO patients was used with a two-step Boruta-LASSO feature selection strategy across five machine learning models to build a mortality-prediction nomogram, externally validated on 22 MIMIC-IV patients. Four predictors (malignant tumor, lactic acid, monocyte-to-white blood cell ratio, and APTT-to-albumin ratio) drove satisfactory discrimination and calibration for bedside risk stratification.

Title: A reliable and explainable deep learning framework for clinical-grade endocrine disorder risk prediction and decision support
Summary: Proposed a Gated Multi-Task Attention Network (GMTAN) that jointly predicts thyroid disorder and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) risk from heterogeneous endocrine datasets, incorporating Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty estimation and SHAP-based explainability. GMTAN achieved AUROC scores of 0.98 (thyroid) and 0.97 (PCOS), outperforming baseline machine learning and deep learning models.
Outcome: thyroid disorder and PCOS risk prediction

Title: A Deep Learning Model Integrating Ultrasound Images and Multidimensional Clinical Information for Differentiating Benign and Malignant Non-Mass Lesions
Summary: A multimodal deep learning network (Image Feature Encoder, Clinical Feature Encoder, and Multi-modal Fusion Decoder) was developed to classify benign versus malignant breast non-mass lesions on ultrasound. The combined model outperformed the image-only model (AUC 0.852 vs. 0.757), with SHAP analysis identifying palpation with indistinct margins, abnormal axillary nodes, and older age as the top malignancy predictors.

Title: A deep residual attention-Recurrent model for early and multi-stage Alzheimer's disease detection
Summary: A hybrid deep learning model (ResNet152V2 with a Convolutional Block Attention Module and a Bidirectional GRU) classified Normal Cognition, Mild Cognitive Impairment, and Alzheimer's Disease using 2,100 ADNI subjects, externally validated on 900 OASIS subjects. The model achieved 94.5% accuracy with an AUC of 0.95 on ADNI and 92.8% accuracy on OASIS, improving 5.2-7.0% over baseline models.

Title: Development and Validation of a Diffusion-weighted Imaging-only Deep Learning Model for the Detection of Supratentorial Acute Ischemic Infarcts: A Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study
Journal/Source: Annals of the Academy of Medicine, Singapore
Summary: A diffusion-weighted-imaging-only deep learning model was trained and tested for automated detection of supratentorial acute ischemic infarcts on MRI, benchmarked against expert radiologist interpretation. The model achieved 90.8% accuracy, 92.1% sensitivity, 89.6% specificity, and an AUC of 0.93, with sub-second processing time per study.

Title: Explainable multi-modal deep learning for transparent cancer diagnosis: integrating radiology, clinical features, and decision visualization
Summary: An explainable multimodal deep learning framework fused radiological imaging and structured clinical features via attention-based fusion, using Grad-CAM++ for image-level explanations and SHAP to quantify clinical feature contributions. The framework was evaluated on CBIS-DDSM, Duke Breast Cancer MRI, and TCGA cohorts (BRCA, LUAD, GBM), totaling 3,842 images from 2,917 patients.
AI Technique: Deep learning (multimodal attention fusion with Grad-CAM++/SHAP)

Title: A clinically deployable deep learning model for automated stroke risk stratification in carotid atherosclerotic plaque
Summary: A ResNet-50 deep learning model analyzing carotid ultrasound images was developed for automated stroke risk stratification in patients with carotid atherosclerotic plaque. The model achieved an AUC of 0.982 (accuracy 0.925, sensitivity 0.964, specificity 0.897) on an independent test set, a 9.7% AUC improvement over the best traditional machine learning model (0.982 vs. 0.885).

Title: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Alzheimer's Diagnosis Using Routine and Low-Cost Clinical Data
Summary: Explainable machine learning models (a deep neural network and a Light Gradient Boosting Machine) diagnosed Alzheimer's disease using only routine, low-cost clinical data (demographics, patient history, neuropsychological tests) from 167,364 observations in the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center dataset. The deep neural network achieved 90% accuracy with ROC-AUC 0.96, while LightGBM reached 90% accuracy with ROC-AUC 0.97, performance comparable to or exceeding clinicians under similar constraints.

Title: Deep Learning Detection of Direct and Indirect Imaging Findings Associated with Pancreatic Cancer at Contrast-enhanced and Noncontrast CT
Summary: Deep learning models were developed to detect direct (pancreatic mass) and indirect (parenchymal atrophy, duct dilatation/stenosis) imaging findings on contrast-enhanced and noncontrast CT for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using retrospective data from 2007-2022. The models achieved AUCs of 0.88-0.95 for individual findings and performed similarly to or better than a six-reader mean for overall diagnosis (CECT AUC 0.99, NCCT AUC 0.93), with markedly higher sensitivity for small (≤20mm) cancers (CECT 98% vs 82.6%; NCCT 86% vs 41.1%).

Title: Development and Validation of an Early Risk Prediction Model for Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy Based on Machine Learning
Summary: Four machine learning models were developed on a retrospective cohort of 197 septic ICU patients (with a 91-patient external validation cohort) using LASSO feature selection to predict early sepsis-induced coagulopathy risk before diagnostic criteria are fully met. The random forest model performed best, achieving internal and external validation AUCs of 0.76 and 0.79, with prolonged PT/APTT, elevated D-dimer, renal insufficiency, and elevated pCO2 increasing risk.
AI Technique: ML (random forest with LASSO feature selection)

Title: Machine learning-based diagnostic model combined with Chinese natural language processing for surgical-site infections: development and validation
Summary: A multicenter cohort study across two tertiary hospitals in China used data from 118,314 surgical patients (June 2023-December 2024), incorporating clinical, microbiological, and demographic variables, to develop machine learning models combined with Chinese NLP for detecting surgical-site infections. The decision tree model achieved an AUC of 0.92 in the development cohort and 0.90 in the validation cohort.

Title: Machine learning screening of risk factors for diabetic microvascular complications and construction of a gradient boosting decision tree predictive model
Summary: Clinical and laboratory data from 1,498 diabetes patients (with and without microvascular complications) were analyzed to identify independent risk factors, including urea, fibrinogen, prothrombin time, D-dimer, CKMB, lipoprotein(a), APTT, triglycerides, and cholinesterase, via collinearity analysis and logistic regression. Nine machine learning models were compared, with the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree model demonstrating superior and consistent AUC and sensitivity across training, validation, and test datasets.

Title: Development and evaluation of a machine learning model to predict unplanned readmission risk in patients with ulcerative colitis
Summary: Eight machine learning models were built on a retrospective cohort (n=324) and validated on an independent prospective cohort (n=137) of ulcerative colitis patients, using demographic, clinical, laboratory, and endoscopic data with recursive feature elimination for feature selection. The random forest model outperformed established clinical scores (Mayo, MES, DUBLIN, UCEIS) for predicting unplanned readmission within one year, with CRP, ESR, RBC, and platelet count among the top contributing features.

Title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning-enabled Single Breath-hold Abbreviated MRI Protocol for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Diagnosis
Summary: A deep learning-based single breath-hold abbreviated MRI protocol (approximately 15 seconds, no contrast agent) was developed and validated in 1,008 patients for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis. The abbreviated protocol showed noninferior diagnostic performance (sensitivity 77.9-88.7%, specificity 91.6-93.1%) compared with conventional full-sequence MRI (sensitivity 84.4-92.5%, specificity 94.1-95.2%), while cutting scan time by over 15 minutes.
AI Technique: Deep learning (single breath-hold abbreviated MRI protocol)

Title: Multicenter Clinical Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Diagnostic Classification Model for Laryngoscopy Images
Summary: A deep learning computer-aided diagnosis model trained on over 20,000 laryngoscopic images from multicenter tertiary referral hospitals in Italy, India, and China was externally validated on Greek and Spanish datasets to distinguish high-risk from low-risk laryngeal lesions. The model achieved accuracy/AUC of 0.90/0.89 internally and 0.85/0.85 and 0.88/0.88 on the external datasets, performing noninferior to otolaryngologists and superior to general practitioners and ChatGPT-4o.
Outcome: laryngeal lesion risk classification (high-risk vs low-risk)

Title: Clinical validation pipeline of a deep learning model for segmenting and quantifying intracranial and ventricular volumes on computed tomography
Summary: DeepCTE3D, a deep convolutional neural network for segmenting and quantifying intracranial and lateral ventricular volumes on CT scans, was validated using a diverse real-world dataset from a large Brazilian hospital spanning multiple scanner models and both normal and pathological cases. The validation pipeline demonstrated a scalable, automated approach for volumetric brain measurement suitable for clinical deployment.

Title: Development and multi-institutional validation of a deep learning algorithm for predicting cervical cord compression using dynamic cervical lateral radiographs
